newsitem.title: USA: No deaths found in New Orleans ship wreck.
newsitem.headline: No deaths found in New Orleans ship wreck.

text.p: Officials said on Monday they were increasingly confident no one had died when a freighter slammed into a New Orleans wharf near the city's French Quarter on Saturday.

"With each passing hour, our confidence grows that in fact we do have a Christmas miracle and we will get through this without any fatalities," Port of New Orleans director Ron Brinson said in a press conference.
Brinson said officials had received reports of two people possibly missing in the crash, but both had been found elsewhere by New Orleans police.

New Orleans Fire Chief Warren McDaniels said the search for possible victims would continue. "We have no reason to believe there's anyone in the rubble, however we are not going to stop until we have searched every part," he told reporters.

The Liberian-flagged freighter Bright Field, carrying a load of 64,000 tons of corn, rammed in to the Riverwalk, a shopping mall on the banks of the Mississippi, when it lost power and the captain was unable to steer it, officials said.

More than 116 people were treated for injuries, many of which were sustained as people fled from the shopping area and the adjacent New Orleans Hilton Hotel. A parking garage and 125 rooms in the hotel were damaged by the ship.
